description:
## Goal

Make compiler warnings demand-driven, supported, retractable facts. Clause coverage has one semantic authority: typed dispatch reachability for demanded activation rows and reached local dispatches. No source-time or whole-contract coverage pass may invent a broader domain or warm cold work.

## End-state laws

- `ActivationInputs` is the sole correlated input evidence for function-head coverage. A contract refines or rejects a reached row; it is never enumerated as an independent coverage domain.
- Local `case` and `with else` coverage uses the typed values reaching that exact lowered dispatch. A `receive` miss remains selection behavior, and `with` without `else` returns the failed value.
- Warning evidence is typed semantic data, never a diagnostic code, message, span, display string, or incidental order.
- The demanded producer contributes warning evidence through its ordinary `AttemptOutcome`/`JobEffects`. Existing World fact claims own OR support and exact last-support retraction; there is no warning-specific ownership graph.
- The current diagnostic snapshot is an ordinary retained product in the existing `ProductMemo` lifecycle. It projects settled semantic evidence through exact source-version provenance and follows exact retained request/product dependencies, never a World/root/source scan.
- A warning never creates semantic demand. Cold functions, unreachable matches, and unobserved contract alternatives do no coverage work.
- Equal reproduction preserves warning evidence and the retained diagnostic allocation/generation, wakes nobody, and performs no deep copy. Delivery may emit that retained snapshot without rerunning a producer.
- No global warning-once registry, source AST coverage walker, contract-domain sweep, duplicate dispatch plan, warning side map, queue/flush, private warning scheduler, compatibility bridge, or reconstruction pass remains.

## Signal

Quicksort is warning-free because every demanded `append/2` and `qsort/1` activation is list-shaped. A reachable non-list row produces exactly one warning; removing its last supporting demand retracts it. Typed `case`/`with else` examples warn only when their reached subject rows can fall through. A location-only replacement updates only diagnostic provenance. Repeating an unchanged request returns the same retained diagnostic snapshot with zero compiler work, allocation, generation change, wake, or deep copy. An unrelated replacement moves nothing for the requested root.

## Strategy

Land vertical cutovers after the source-owner, completed-attempt, semantic-support, live-replacement, diagnostic-provenance, and product-request lifecycle foundations.

The first child is deliberately atomic: it establishes the typed warning-evidence contribution, one retained diagnostic-snapshot product, and the first function-head producer together. Splitting those would require either an invisible fact with no production consumer or a temporary queue/scan bridge. Later children migrate producers into that final model and delete the authorities they replace.

Before implementation, fz-kdt.36.1 must prove on paper how a warning key, value, producer contribution, provenance dependency, request membership, and retained snapshot fit the existing World fact ledger and ProductMemo without a second store or cone. If that model cannot be finite, exact, and scan-free, update the ticket before landing code.

The closeout blocks source-version reclamation so warning provenance participates in the ownership proof before old versions can be freed.

## Existing tickets absorbed or refined

- fz-kdt.36 becomes this epic; its former policy choice is resolved in favor of demanded activation evidence.
- fz-5xp.88 owns actionable rendering from reachable typed failure evidence.
- fz-tfn.40 supplies content/provenance separation; it does not own warning support.
- fz-tfn.46 supplies completed attempt outputs and exact replacement of claims/observations.
- fz-kdt.64 supplies exact withdrawal of supported `ActivationInputs` alternatives.
- fz-tfn.47 supplies the single retained request/ProductMemo lifecycle.
- fz-kdt.37 is a later warning producer and must consume this completed model rather than recreate the deleted accumulator.
- fz-tfn.58 is obsolete because fz-5xp.87 already delivered its runtime-helper contract scope; those specs are not the semantic authority for coverage.

One child equals one commit and one close. Every child updates affected agent/user docs and removes its own construction debris.

## Accepted child DAG

- fz-kdt.36.1 — atomic warning-fact/retained-snapshot/function-head vertical slice; removes source-head and whole-contract coverage.
- fz-kdt.36.2 — typed local `case`/`with else` coverage in the same activation attempt; removes the source AST coverage walker.
- fz-kdt.36.3 — side-effect-free resolver warning migration; deletes the global warning queue/flush lifecycle.
- fz-5xp.88 — typed canonical reachable failure witnesses and construct-correct remedies.
- fz-kdt.36.4 — exact reuse/retraction proof, debris removal, and final documentation.

Direct dependencies are authoritative in bw:

```text
tfn.40 + tfn.47 -> kdt.36.1
kdt.36.1 -> kdt.36.2 -> 5xp.88
kdt.36.1 -> kdt.36.3
kdt.36.3 + 5xp.88 -> kdt.36.4 -> tfn.20
kdt.36.4 -> kdt.37
```
title: Demand-driven retractable warning facts: collapse clause coverage into semantic analysis
